title: Racial Traits
text: “Honestly, I keep wondering, where exactly does Luna-chan draw the line for ‘cute,’ anyway?”
“Imiya and the others did say the Rumo-species folks were cute, but they didn’t seem nearly as interested as when they looked at Ren-san, did they?”
“It hugged my kid like it was completely smitten, cooing about how cute they were.”
“Those children are babies, though. Maybe it was holding back.”
Thinking about Luna-chan’s state of mind, my heart nearly split in two. Luna-chan was either carrying Keel around, or perched atop Keel’s head in chick mode.
“Also, Motoyasu-san let out a rather strange noise, didn’t he?”
“At a glance, didn’t it look like it was… unwell? Given that fierce look on its face, that’s the only way I could take it.”
“Ahh… that’s Motoyasu-kun’s weak point, isn’t it.”
“Hiiiii… I say!”
“If Luna-chan saw Motoyasu-kun like this right now, it’d probably scoop him up out of pure joy.”
Hiiiiiiii… I say.
“If at all possible, I’d like to offer up Motoyasu as a sacrifice and make my escape.”
“In that case, it sounds like it’d turn into an epic tug-of-war between it and Yuki-chan over Motoyasu-kun. Yuki-chan might end up going a little unwell too.”
“Y-Yuki-chan wouldn’t do something like that, I say!”
“Well, Yuki-san strikes me as more of the athletic-noble-girl type, honestly—someone whose motto is freshness and elegance.”
“Yuki-chan’s super popular on the racing circuit, you know. Her loyalty to Motoyasu-kun is probably a cut above the rest.”
“Come to think of it, Motoyasu-san apparently isn’t great with the ‘unwell’ types, but were there really no other Filolials like that besides Filo-san?”

At that moment, a memory suddenly resurfaced—of Ku-chan once giving me that same sort of look, sending a chill down my spine—but no, it must have just been my imagination. She’d always been perfectly cheerful with Midori and Marine-chan. Ahh… Luna-chan. I wanted so badly to free her from those eyes as soon as possible. Ren, you need to heal Luna-chan more than that! I’ll make absolutely certain you become her designated healer! With that resolve burning in my chest, I pressed onward, and before long we emerged into some kind of open space. Up ahead, there seemed to be a staircase.
“What do you suppose this is? This space practically screaming ‘a boss is here,’ I mean.”
“Isn’t that exactly what it is?”
Just then, a Karma Dog appeared from out of nowhere with a sudden thud.
“Bow!”
“Feels like a proper boss entrance.”
“Shall we open with a preemptive strike?”
Bang! Itsuki unleashed a merciless volley of gunfire straight at the Karma Dog, and it went down without a fight.
“Kyaun!?”
“Wiped it out before its lackeys even showed up.”
“Guess we can just say Karma Dogs count as small fry in front of us, properly leveled up as we are.”
“I mean, easy is nice and all, but is this really okay?”
“Next one’s mine—I’ll finish it in a flash, I say.”
The fallen Karma Dog dissolved away like mist, and the smoke was drawn into our weapons. Oh? I could confirm a drop item.
“Motoyasu-kun, something about what you just said feels off, too… actually, what even is this place, really?”
“Back in the game days, this was content where you fought a boss on a specific floor. No real payoff in experience points, and no drops either.”
“Confirmed properly this time, though. Seems this one’s just a simple weapon-and-gear drop from the Karma Dog series.”
“Mostly stuff we already have, though—kind of underwhelming. I guess the deeper we go, the stronger the enemies get?”
“That’s highly likely. In any case, let’s move on to the next floor.”
And so, having cleared floor one, we pressed onward to the next.
As we advanced, Ren’s nose started twitching.
“What’s wrong?”
“Hm? Ah… thought I caught a whiff of medicine or something.”
“Medicine?”
At Father’s question, Ren approached the cave wall to investigate. It seemed he’d spotted some medicinal herbs peeking out from a crack in the wall.
“So that’s what the smell was—medicinal herbs.”
“Ren, seems like turning into an Inult form sharpened your nose.”
“Seems that way… gives me complicated feelings, honestly.”
“Right, right, speaking of which—about the reason we all ended up in these forms—maybe this dungeon has some kind of mechanism where everyone has to make use of their own racial traits?”
At Father’s words, both Ren and Itsuki made sour faces.
“There wasn’t anything like that back in the game era, but the fact that we can’t rule it out is the annoying part. And Ren-san did just find those herbs.”
“True enough. So if we think about it that way, what kind of gimmick seems likely? In my case, it’d be smell, I guess…”
“Hmm, Itsuki’s a squirrel-type, so maybe tree-climbing?”
“Admittedly, in this form, climbing walls would be a lot easier than in a human body, but…”
By the way, all of us were currently in our respective cosplay-transformed states.
“So you’d be gliding, then, I say.”
“That’s a flying squirrel thing, not a regular squirrel!”
“Setting Motoyasu’s joke aside, if some floor requires tree-climbing, I guess we’ll be relying on Itsuki.”
“I’d really rather that not happen. Besides, if Motoyasu-san just flies in flying mode, wouldn’t that make it unnecessary anyway?”
“Speaking as though it’s a given that Motoyasu-kun can fly…”
“Leave it to me, I say.”
This Motoyasu, after all, was always researching and refining his craft. Flying through the sky as a means of travel was child’s play.
“Well, honestly, when it comes to flying, I think Itsuki can probably do it too, so tree-climbing might not be strictly necessary.”
“Why do you assume I can fly!?”

“Eh? I mean, your weapon comes equipped with guns too, right? If you fully upgraded a pair of flamethrower pistols and fired them both straight down at the ground, wouldn’t you just kind of float up?”
“Eh?”

Itsuki stepped a short distance away, casually dual-wielded a pair of pistols, and fired flame bursts down at the ground. With a great WHOOOOSH, he lifted right up into the air. Eventually he landed with a soft thud and turned to stare at the rest of us.
“Don’t look at me like that.”
Ren cut in with the retort. Hmm… Itsuki really did seem like the one best suited for flying.
“Naofumi-san! How could you say something like that!”
“I mean, the fact that you actually tried it says something too, doesn’t it?”

“If you’re going to say that, then surely both Naofumi-san and Ren-san must have some way of flying too! In Naofumi-san’s case, something board-related seems plausible—like some kind of hoverboard! And come to think of it, couldn’t you ride waves with that shield of yours or something?”
“I’ve always wondered about it whenever I looked at the ocean!” Itsuki said, his tone thoroughly flustered.
“I’ll admit turning the shield into a surfboard is something I’ve considered before, but a hoverboard? This isn’t some anime…”
“And in Ren-san’s case…”
Itsuki trailed off, apparently unable to come up with anything. Then, as if struck by sudden inspiration, he spoke up.
“Couldn’t you use a floating sword as a foothold and fly that way!?”
“I’m not even that good with floating swords to begin with, and even if I tried standing on one, it wouldn’t make me fly.”

“In Ren’s case… isn’t there something like that? If there’s some sword with a legend about flying attached to it, that’d probably work. In some old manga I know, there was a protagonist who flew using a sword that housed a dragon god, or one with a thunder god sealed inside.”
“Stop it! Not everything has to be capable of flight just because you say so.”
“It’s a parade of flying heroes here. If anything, as a Sacred Weapon hero, that much should be a given, shouldn’t it?”
Itsuki declared this as if he’d thrown caution entirely to the wind. The trouble was, given his current squirrel form, it came across as thoroughly absurd.
“Well, it’s true that back in the very first world, Father did end up able to fly.”
“The me right now is a penguin that can’t fly—Peckle, pen.”
Father answered with his chest puffed out, just as defiantly. Penguins certainly can’t fly, but if it’s Father, I have faith he could manage it somehow.
“Playing dumb won’t save you from this one, Naofumi-san.”
“Enough joking around—so seriously, what would it even feel like for me to fly?”
“Quite literally, I say? Something about learning to use your power in a certain way lets you fly, apparently.”

Father had come back having mastered a power of an entirely different lineage from the Crimson Swine herself. Now that I think of it… some time after that battle, I recall certain people showing up to teach Father and the others how to use that power.
